tagline: Kenya. Wild. Alive. — From the Savannah to the Ocean
about: Utamaduni Safaris was born in Kombani, a small town in Kwale County, from the friendship of two young men who grew up surrounded by Kenya's most incredible natural wonders. Salim and Abdallah saw the beauty of Shimba Hills, the magic of the coast, and the richness of Swahili culture — and decided the world needed to experience it too.
address: Kombani, Matuga Sub-County, Kwale County, Kenya

destinations.title: Shimba Hills National Reserve
destinations.short: Coastal rainforest, elephants & Kenya's only sable antelope.
destinations.description: Just inland from the coast, Shimba Hills protects one of East Africa's last large coastal rainforests. Home to elephants, the rare sable antelope, and the beautiful Sheldrick Falls. A hidden gem only an hour from Diani Beach.

destinations.title: Diani & Tiwi Beaches
destinations.short: Powder-white sands and turquoise Indian Ocean waters.
destinations.description: Diani Beach is repeatedly voted among Africa's best beaches. Long stretches of soft white sand, calm lagoons for snorkelling, kitesurfing, colobus monkey forests, and relaxed Swahili coastal life make it truly special.

destinations.title: Kisite-Mpunguti Marine Park
destinations.short: Dolphins, coral reefs and dhow sailing to Wasini Island.
destinations.description: Kenya's premier marine park. Snorkel vibrant reefs, swim with wild spinner dolphins, sail traditional dhows and enjoy fresh crab and coconut seafood on car-free Wasini Island. An unforgettable ocean experience.

destinations.title: Kaya Forests & Cultural Heritage
destinations.short: Sacred Mijikenda forests and living coastal heritage.
destinations.description: Guided walks into sacred kaya forests with community elders. Learn about traditional beliefs, healing plants, conservation practices, local dances and Swahili coastal cuisine. The Kaya forests are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

destinations.title: Maasai Mara National Reserve
destinations.short: The Great Migration and Africa's most iconic safari destination.
destinations.description: The Maasai Mara is Kenya's most celebrated reserve, home to the annual wildebeest migration, the Big Five, and spectacular open savannah landscapes. The river crossings between July and October are the greatest wildlife spectacle on Earth.

destinations.title: Amboseli National Park
destinations.short: Elephants against the backdrop of mighty Mount Kilimanjaro.
destinations.description: Amboseli offers some of Africa's most iconic views — massive elephant herds roaming freely beneath the snow-capped peak of Mount Kilimanjaro. A UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a photographer's paradise.

destinations.title: Tsavo East & West
destinations.short: Kenya's largest park — red elephants, lava flows and vast wilderness.
destinations.description: Tsavo is Kenya's largest national park system. Famous for its distinctive red-dusted elephants, the crystal-clear Mzima Springs, dramatic Lugard Falls, and incredible biodiversity stretching across 21,000 square kilometres of wilderness.

destinations.title: Mount Kenya & Surroundings
destinations.short: Africa's second-highest peak — trekking, glaciers and unique alpine wildlife.
destinations.description: Mount Kenya offers dramatic trekking routes through bamboo forests, moorlands and glaciated peaks. The surrounding national park is home to buffalo, leopard, and the rare mountain bongo antelope in breathtaking highland scenery.

destinations.title: Lake Nakuru National Park
destinations.short: Flamingos, rhinos and a lake that turns pink.
destinations.description: Lake Nakuru is famous for its stunning flamingo flocks that colour the water pink. The park is also one of Kenya's most reliable places to spot both black and white rhinos, Rothschild giraffe and tree-climbing lions.

destinations.title: Samburu National Reserve
destinations.short: Rare northern species in a dramatic semi-arid landscape.
destinations.description: Samburu is home to the 'Samburu Special Five' — Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, Somali ostrich, Beisa oryx and gerenuk. Set in a stunning semi-arid landscape along the Ewaso Ng'iro River, it's a magical destination.

destinations.title: Hell's Gate National Park
destinations.short: Cycle through gorges, geysers and dramatic cliffs — no car needed.
destinations.description: Hell's Gate is Kenya's most unique park — you can cycle or hike through it without a vehicle. Dramatic volcanic cliffs, Ol Njorowa Gorge, Fischer's Tower, and natural geothermal geysers make it unforgettable for adventurers.

destinations.title: Lamu Island
destinations.short: UNESCO-listed Swahili city, dhow sailing and pristine beaches.
destinations.description: Lamu Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site — Kenya's oldest living Swahili settlement. No cars, only donkeys and dhows. Stunning beaches, fresh seafood and a timeless coastal atmosphere that feels centuries removed from the modern world.

destinations.title: Watamu Marine Park
destinations.short: Sea turtles, world-class diving and pristine coral reefs.
destinations.description: Watamu is a marine biodiversity hotspot. The marine national park protects nesting sea turtles, vibrant coral gardens, tropical fish, and offers some of East Africa's best snorkelling and diving. The Blue Cave is a highlight.

destinations.title: Malindi & Gedi Ruins
destinations.short: Historic Swahili coast town with beaches, heritage and marine life.
destinations.description: Malindi blends Portuguese colonial history with Swahili coastal culture. Visit the Vasco da Gama pillar, snorkel the marine park, then explore the mysterious 15th-century ruins of Gede — a lost city hidden in the coastal forest.

destinations.title: Fort Jesus Museum — Mombasa
destinations.short: UNESCO World Heritage fortress guarding 400 years of East African history.
destinations.description: Built by the Portuguese in 1593, Fort Jesus is one of the most outstanding and well-preserved examples of 16th-century Portuguese military architecture. Now a UNESCO World Heritage Site and national museum, it houses artefacts from the Swahili, Arab, Portuguese, and British eras. The old town surrounding it is a living museum of Swahili coastal culture.

destinations.title: Gede Ruins — Watamu
destinations.short: A lost 15th-century Swahili city swallowed by the coastal forest.
destinations.description: Hidden within the Arabuko-Sokoke Forest near Watamu, the ruins of Gede are one of Kenya's most haunting and atmospheric heritage sites. This prosperous Swahili trading town, abandoned mysteriously in the 17th century, features mosques, palaces, houses and tombs reclaimed by ancient trees. A truly magical step back in time.

destinations.title: Arabuko-Sokoke Forest
destinations.short: East Africa's largest coastal forest — rare birds, golden-rumped elephant shrews.
destinations.description: Arabuko-Sokoke is the largest surviving coastal forest in East Africa and a globally Important Bird & Biodiversity Area. It shelters over 230 bird species including three endemic species found nowhere else on Earth, plus the golden-rumped elephant shrew, Aders' duiker, and the rare Sokoke scops owl. The forest borders the Gede Ruins and Mida Creek — a perfect full-day nature combination.

destinations.title: Kakamega Rainforest
destinations.short: Kenya's only rainforest — a Congo Basin relic full of primates and rare birds.
destinations.description: Kakamega Forest is Kenya's only tropical rainforest — a magnificent relic of the ancient Guineo-Congolian forest that once stretched from West Africa. It is home to primates including red-tailed monkeys, colobus, and baboons, over 330 bird species, rare butterflies, and giant trees draped in moss and ferns. Guided walks and canopy viewing are unforgettable.

destinations.title: Karura Forest — Nairobi
destinations.short: An urban forest paradise — waterfalls, caves and cycling trails inside Nairobi.
destinations.description: Karura Forest is a remarkable 1,041-hectare gazetted forest right inside Nairobi city — one of the world's largest urban forests. Home to colobus monkeys, bushbuck, and over 200 bird species. Walk or cycle through bamboo groves, discover hidden waterfalls, and explore old colonial-era caves, all minutes from the city centre.

destinations.title: Nairobi National Museum
destinations.short: Kenya's premier museum — culture, history, art and natural history in one place.
destinations.description: The Nairobi National Museum is Kenya's most comprehensive museum, housing exhibits on natural history, Kenya's diverse cultures and peoples, prehistoric fossils from the Great Rift Valley, contemporary East African art, and the remarkable story of human evolution. The adjacent Snake Park and botanical gardens add to a full day of discovery.

adventures.title: Shimba Hills Safari
adventures.description: Game drive through one of East Africa's last coastal rainforests. Sable antelope, elephants & Sheldrick Falls. Picnic lunch included.

adventures.title: Dhow & Dolphin — Kisite-Mpunguti
adventures.description: Sail a traditional dhow to Wasini Island, snorkel coral reefs, swim with wild dolphins, and feast on fresh crab and coconut seafood lunch.

adventures.title: Kaya Forest Cultural Immersion
adventures.description: Walk sacred Mijikenda kaya forests with community elders. Traditional dances, healing plants & authentic Swahili cuisine.

adventures.title: Mwaluganje Elephant Sanctuary
adventures.description: Drive or walk through Kenya's community-owned elephant conservancy. Free-roaming elephants, rare birds and inspiring conservation stories.

adventures.title: Diani & Tiwi Beach Escape
adventures.description: Relax on Africa's finest white-sand beach. Kitesurf intro, colobus monkey forest walk, and sunset dhow cocktail cruise included.

adventures.title: Maasai Mara Migration Safari
adventures.description: Witness the greatest wildlife spectacle — millions of wildebeest and zebra crossing the Mara River. Big Five, Maasai village & optional hot-air balloon.

adventures.title: Amboseli Elephants & Kilimanjaro
adventures.description: Photograph elephant families beneath snow-capped Kilimanjaro. Africa's most iconic landscape and a photographer's ultimate dream.

adventures.title: Samburu Northern Frontier
adventures.description: Discover the rare 'Samburu Special Five' in a dramatic semi-arid landscape along the Ewaso Ng'iro River.

adventures.title: Hell's Gate Cycling Adventure
adventures.description: Cycle through Africa's most unique national park — volcanic cliffs, gorges, geothermal geysers. No game-drive vehicle needed.

adventures.title: Lamu Island Cultural Retreat
adventures.description: Dhow to a UNESCO World Heritage Site with no cars — ancient Swahili architecture, pristine beaches and the finest fresh seafood.

adventures.title: Tsavo Red Elephant Wilderness
adventures.description: Kenya's largest park — red-dusted elephants, Mzima Springs, Lugard Falls and vast untouched wilderness.

adventures.title: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino
adventures.description: Watch the lake turn pink with flamingos. Kenya's most reliable spot for black & white rhinos, Rothschild giraffe and tree-climbing lions.

adventures.title: Mombasa Old Town & Fort Jesus
adventures.description: Walk the streets of Mombasa Old Town with an expert guide. UNESCO Fort Jesus, spice markets, ancient mosques and street food.

adventures.title: Malindi Marine Park & Gedi Ruins
adventures.description: Snorkel spectacular coral gardens then explore the mysterious 15th-century ruins of Gede — a lost Swahili city hidden in the coastal forest.

adventures.title: Utamaduni Grand Circuit
adventures.description: The ultimate Kenya experience — a custom circuit combining wildlife parks, marine adventures and cultural immersion across the entire country.
